earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 newmontq32026earningsrelea.htm EX-99.1 Document NYSE: NEM, ASX: NEM, PNGX: NEM EXHIBIT 99.1 Newmont Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results with Record Third Quarter Adjusted Net Income; Positioned to Achieve Full-Year Guidance; Provides Update on Red Chris Block Cave Project DENVER, October 22, 2026 – Newmont Corporation (NYSE: NEM, ASX: NEM, PNGX: NEM) (Newmont or the Company) today announced third quarter 2026 results and declared a dividend of $0.26 1 per share. "Newmont remains on track to achieve our full-year 2026 production guidance and improved full-year cost outlook, supported by disciplined operational execution in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength and resilience of our world-class portfolio," said Natascha Viljoen, Newmont's President and Chief Executive Officer. "We produced approximately 1.3 million attributable gold ounces, and generated $1.9 billion of free cash flow. Since our last earnings call, we have returned $1.9 billion to shareholders through quarterly dividends and share repurchases, contributing to an approximate 10% reduction in our total share count since February 2024, reflecting our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders on a per-share basis.” Q3 2026 Results ▪ On track to meet Newmont's full-year 2026 production guidance 2 of 5.3 million attributable gold ounces; produced 1.3 million attributable gold ounces, as well as 11 million ounces of silver and 23 thousand tonnes of copper, primarily from Newmont's managed operations ▪ Gold by-product Costs Applicable to Sales (CAS) was $832 per ounce and All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC) was $1,454 per ounce 3 ; improved full-year cost guidance to $925 and $1,520 per ounce, respectively 2 ▪ Reported Net Income of $2.5 billion, Adjusted Net Income (ANI) 3 of $2.3 billion or $2.20 per diluted share, and Adjusted EBITDA 3 of $4.0 billion ▪ Generated $2.8 billion of cash from operating activities, net of working capital impacts of $565 million; reported third quarter Free Cash Flow 3 of $1.9 billion ▪ Delivered $1.9 billion of shareholder returns through share repurchases and dividend payments since the last earnings call 4 ; declared a dividend of $0.26 per share of common stock for the third quarter of 2026 ▪ Through the date of filing, Newmont has repurchased $1.6 billion of common stock since the last earnings call 4 ; $2.8 billion remains under the current authorized program of $6.0 billion 5 ▪ Since February 2024, Newmont has reduced its share count by over 115 million shares, or approximately 10 percent of shares outstanding, increasing shareholders' exposure to the free cash flow generated by its portfolio and creating a pathway for per-share dividend growth over time ▪ Ended the quarter with $8.8 billion of cash and $12.8 billion in total liquidity 6 , with a net cash position of $3.2 billion 3 ▪ Announced an amended agreement for the Nevada Gold Mines Joint Venture (NGM) to include the contribution of previously excluded assets including Barrick's Fourmile and Newmont's Fiberline and Mike ▪ Advancing the Red Chris Block Cave towards a full-funds investment decision in early 2027; finalizing feasibility study, subject to review and governance oversight; provided update on key project metrics and timeline 7 ▪ Completed shaft construction at Tanami Expansion 2; advancing project ahead of schedule, with commercial production now expected in the first half of 2027 7 1 Newmont's Board of Directors declared a dividend of $0.26 per share of common stock for the third quarter of 2026, payable on December 21, 2026 to holders of record at the close of business on November 25, 2026. 2 For further details see the '2026 Guidance Expectations' section below, as well as the discussion of guidance and cautionary statement at the end of this release regarding forward-looking statements. 3 Non-GAAP metrics; see reconciliations at the end of this release. 4 Includes $1.6 billion of share repurchases since July 23, 2026, including approximately $451 million of share repurchases in October 2026. 5 The share repurchase program will be executed at the Company's discretion. The share repurchase program permits shares to be repurchased in a variety of methods, has no time limit and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. See cautionary statement regarding forward-looking statements at end of this release. 6 Total liquidity as of September 30, 2026 includes $4.0 billion available on a revolving credit facility. 7 For further details see the 'Projects Update' section below, as well as the cautionary statement at the end of this release regarding forward-looking statements. NEWMONT THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS | NEWS RELEASE 1 Delivering on Newmont's Consistent Capital Allocation Framework Newmont's consistent capital allocation framework is designed to be sustainable through the commodity and investment cycles while maximizing total return of capital to shareholders, maintaining a flexible and resilient balance sheet, and focusing on high-return capital investments for long-term value creation. The capital allocation uses below are presented in order of priority. 1 Newmont is consistently delivering on these priorities, supported by the robust free cash flow generated to date in 2026. Ongoing Sustaining Capital Investment in World-Class Portfolio Newmont expects to spend $1.95 billion in 2026 in sustaining capital through targeted investments in critical infrastructure, including tailings solutions, as detailed in the '2026 Guidance Expectations' section below. As of the end of the third quarter, Newmont has invested $1.33 billion of sustaining capital in 2026, with full-year 2026 guidance remaining unchanged. 2 Sustainable Through the Cycle Cash Dividend Newmont is committed to returning capital to shareholders through a sustainable cash dividend of $1.1 billion per year. Central to this framework is a dividend structured to grow on a per-share basis without increasing Newmont's financial commitment, as share repurchases executed through the cycle permanently lower the outstanding share count. The annual total per share dividend target will be calculated annually in February based on the current number of shares issued and outstanding. The dividend payment will be divided into four equal payments rounded up to the nearest $0.01, to be paid out on a quarterly basis, subject to quarterly approval by Newmont's Board of Directors 1 . In line with this commitment, a dividend of $0.26 per share for the third quarter of 2026 has been declared payable on December 21, 2026, to holders of record of such common stock at the close of business on November 25, 2026. This equates to an indicated total annualized dividend of $1.04 per share, with continued per-share dividend increases expected as share repurchases continue. Disciplined Approach to Development Capital Reinvestment Newmont expects to invest $1.4 billion of development capital in 2026 as it advances the highest-return free cash flow generative projects, while continuing to study, evaluate and define the future growth profile of its portfolio. As of the end of the third quarter, Newmont has invested $878 million in its current development projects in 2026, with full-year 2026 guidance remaining unchanged. 2 Maintaining an Optimized Capital Structure Through the Cycle Newmont is focused on maintaining a resilient balance sheet, anchored by a $1 billion net cash target 3 , with flexibility of plus or minus $2 billion depending on market conditions. During strong commodity price environments, Newmont intends to further optimize its balance sheet by actively managing gross debt, while maintaining a minimum cash balance of $5 billion through the cycle. Newmont ended the third quarter of 2026 with a cash balance of $8.8 billion and a net cash balance of $3.2 billion 3 , before the planned payment of $1.95 billion to Barrick under the terms of the amended NGM agreement, which is expected to be paid in the fourth quarter. Ratable Share Repurchase Program Since the last earnings call, Newmont executed $1.6 billion of share repurchases, with $2.8 billion remaining under the current repurchase authorization of $6.0 billion. Newmont intends to request additional approval from its Board of Directors as the current authorization approaches completion, consistent with the Company's disciplined and repeatable approach to returning excess cash to shareholders. 1 See cautionary statement at the end of this release. The Capital Allocation Framework is provided for illustrative purposes and remains non-binding. Guidance expectations, including capital allocation uses, future dividends, debt management and share repurchases, are forward-looking statements. An annualized dividend has not been declared by the Board of Directors. 2 Capital expenditures are shown on an attributable basis, exclusive of capitalized interest, and therefore will not directly agree to Additions to property plant and mine development from the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows. 3 Net cash balance is Cash and cash equivalents less Debt and Lease and other financing obligations as presented on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. Net cash balance will change based on Net cash provided by operating activities , Additions to property, plant and mine development , dividends paid to common shareholders, repayment of debt principal, and other investing and financing activities. reference.summary: Newmont Corporation operates as a gold producer. It also explores for copper, silver, lead, zinc, and other metals. It has operations and/or assets in the United States, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Ghana, Suriname, Argentina, Dominican Republic, Chile, Peru, Ecuador, Mexico, and Canada. The company was founded in 1916 and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.
